trust_decision.summary: The method string taken from an HTTP request is used verbatim as the low-cardinality 'method' tag (and, for Jersey observation, as the contextual/span name), so arbitrary method tokens create unbounded meters; the fix decides, inside each tag/name builder, to emit the request method only when it is one of the nine RFC 9110/5789 standard methods and otherwise return the cached METHOD_UNKNOWN.

landing_point.why: Reading only 'Micrometer HTTP server instrumentations DoS', an engineer lands on the core http binder helper that turns a servlet request into the 'method' Tag used when a server Timer is registered.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The jetty12 provider is a separate optional module implementing Jetty's non-servlet core API, and client-side helpers take the method from the local caller, so a solver can argue the report's servlet example defines the covered surface and neither was ever in scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Standard methods must keep their exact raw tag/name value ('GET' stays 'GET', span name stays 'HTTP GET'); an over-broad 'always UNKNOWN', truncation or case-normalising fix destroys per-method metrics and span names for all normal traffic.

O6_input_shapes: null request -> METHOD_UNKNOWN (null handling preserved, @Nullable added)
standard uppercase method (GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, DELETE, CONNECT, OPTIONS, TRACE, PATCH) -> raw value kept
case variant of a standard method (e.g. 'get') -> UNKNOWN (check is case-sensitive)
empty or whitespace method string -> UNKNOWN
request object whose getMethod() returns null -> UNKNOWN (Set.contains(null) is false)
